item.title: Security Policy
item.description:
EximeeBPMS is an open-source BPMN 2.0 process automation platform, forked from Camunda 7 and maintained by Consdata. It is used to run business-critical, and in some cases regulated, workloads, so the security of the software is treated as a top priority.

This page is a summary. The canonical, version-controlled policy — including supported versions, how to report a vulnerability, our response process, scope, and legal notice — lives in SECURITY.md in the main EximeeBPMS repository. If anything here ever appears to conflict with SECURITY.md, SECURITY.md is authoritative.

item.title: Operating EximeeBPMS Securely
item.description:
The instructions how to operate EximeeBPMS securely are located in our User Guide. Make sure to read the version of the user guide that matches the EximeeBPMS version you use.

To report a security issue rather than harden a deployment, see Report a Vulnerability.

item.title: Security Notices
item.description:
On this page, EximeeBPMS publishes security notices after fixes are available. Fixes are available as EximeeBPMS patch or minor releases. See SECURITY.md for our reporting process and disclosure timeline.

EximeeBPMS notices

Notice EXBPMS-19

Publication Date: November 2, 2026

Product affected: EximeeBPMS Run, in both its default (default.yml) and production (production.yml) configuration, including the Docker images built from it. The Tomcat and WildFly distributions and the Spring Boot starter do not ship this setting.

item.title: Report a Vulnerability
item.description:
Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.

To report a vulnerability in EximeeBPMS, use GitHub’s private vulnerability reporting feature:

github.com/EximeeBPMS/eximeebpms/security/advisories/new

This opens a private draft security advisory visible only to the maintainers.

When reporting, please include:

  • The affected component/module and version(s) (e.g. engine, REST API, Cockpit/Admin/Tasklist, eximeebpms-run)
  • A description of the vulnerability and its potential impact
  • Steps to reproduce, or a proof of concept
  • Any known workaround

We acknowledge new reports within 3 business days. See SECURITY.md for our full process, supported versions, scope, and coordinated-disclosure expectations.
